title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

reports.title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

summary:
Two sisters from Rio Arriba County are suing Española after police stopped them on July 23. A Flock Safety camera misread their license plate, confusing a final 2 for a 7, and flagged the car as stolen from Rio Rancho. Officers pulled over Jaclynn Gonzales, 21, and her 12-year-old sister on Calle Duran, handcuffed both, and placed them in separate police vehicles before realizing the error. Jaclynn had asked police to call their mother, who lived nearby, but the girl was still handcuffed and detained.

The lawsuits, filed Jan. 3, seek unspecified damages for anxiety, fear, and restriction of movement. Their attorney, Sheri Raphaelson, also represents Adam Pacheco, a 17-year-old honor student who was wrongly stopped in a similar camera-related mistake. The city, police chief, and Flock Safety did not respond to requests for comment. The cases will proceed in state District Court.
